title: I asked Astra to animate a spider for me
author: This-Memory4929
selftext:
Hey everyone, recently I wanted to animate a spider for my game, but dealing with all those legs was becoming a nightmare.

So at some point I decided to ask Astra to do it for me.

I prepared a prompt with the things I needed and asked for 4 animations: idle, walk, attack and death.

This is the result.

Honestly, I was pretty surprised. I think it turned out really well. Only problem: it basically burned through all 5 hours of my Plus plan 😅

I guess if I want to keep making more of these, I’m going to need an upgrade.

replies.author: This-Memory4929
replies.body:
If you mean the workflow, I basically started with the spider model and asked Astra to handle the rig and animations.

**Idle:** small movements of the body and abdomen, with subtle movements of the pedipalps and chelicerae. Keep the tips of the legs planted on the ground.

**Walk:** walk in place using two alternating groups of four legs. Define the foot trajectories first, separating the planted phase from the lifted recovery phase. Keep at least four legs on the ground at all times, with smooth lifts and no sudden snapping. During the planted phase, move the feet backward at a constant speed to match the character’s forward movement in-game.

**Attack:** anticipation by lowering the body, raising the front legs, then a forward lunge and bite with the chelicerae, followed by a return to the starting pose.

**Death:** the body collapses while all the legs progressively fold inward before the spider rolls over, then holds the final pose. Avoid having extended legs unnaturally lift the body off the ground.

So basically, if you already have the model, you just need to be fairly clear about the movement and the constraints you want for the legs.

comments.author: Original-League-6094
comments.body: That's really good. The death animation was cute. A pro-tip I only just realized: It can lift frames from youtube videos. So if you find a clean video of a spider walking, you can tell Astra to view the video, extra a frame by frame walk cycle, and then animate from there.

replies.author: This-Memory4929
replies.body: I didn’t know that, I’ll have to try it. Thanks for the tip 😉

ExtremeCenterism

replies.author: This-Memory4929
replies.body: It burned through 5 hours of my Plus plan. The cost is pretty high, and I still haven’t figured out how to reduce it.

comments.author: zodyXL
comments.body: Eu estou querendo pedir para o ASTRAL animar um dragão. e queria sua opinião, voce acha melhor usar um prompt bem detalhado sobre oque eu quero? ou eu pensei em criar uma imegem tipo um sprit sheet sabe mostrando as animações que eu quero, e alem do propt tambem a imagem, voce acha que a imagem ajudaria?

replies.author: This-Memory4929
replies.body: It depends on what you want to use it for. An image definitely helps as a reference, and a well-detailed prompt will certainly help you get better animations. So if you want to create a highly detailed dragon, I’d recommend giving it as much information and reference material as you can.

comments.body: You should consider asking it to do programmatic IK animations that smoothly adjust between surface angles instead. Thank me later.
